Summary of customer type by hour in FY25 Q4. 14 4. PREVENTATIVE MAINTENANCE MANAGEMENT AT THE NSTTF Preventative maintenance (PM) is essential to maintaining a reliable, safe, and available NSTTF. In FY25, the NSTTF continued development and deployment of a computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to strengthen work control, increase consistency in PM execution, and improve our understanding of corrective maintenance drivers and downtime. This year’s efforts focused on expanding Maximo asset coverage across major site capabilities, improving maintenance processes and job plans, and maturing performance tracking to better support an R&D test facility. 4.1. Maximo Expansion The NSTTF’s heliostat field and solar furnace facility are now captured in Maximo, with 274 assets currently managed and tracked. Progressing Maximo from the initial pilot capabilities to broader site implementation are the next steps, with assets from the solar tower documented and their site criticality to NSTTF operations assessed. This establishes a foundation for structured maintenance and PM planning within Maximo. Training materials for Maximo were created for NSTTF personnel to improve consistency of use and data quality. 4.2. Preventative Maintenance Execution FY25 PM planning and execution were organized around two PM tracks — electrical and mechanical — to utilize our technologist capabilities and improve schedule flow. Overall scheduled mechanical PM completion was impacted by competing mission- critical G3P3 construction with 15% completed for the year. Despite work being diverted to solar furnace repairs, 63% of scheduled electrical PMs for our heliostat field were completed. The solar furnace repair was the most significant corrective maintenance campaign in FY25. During this effort, NSTTF also addressed a key reliability contributor: spare part tracking and storage.
